en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section First Chapter
Discourse on the Foundations of Mindfulness:
Are all phenomena the foundations of mindfulness?
Yes, they are.
All phenomena are mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the mindfulness factor of enlightenment;

they are the one-way path, leading to destruction, leading to awakening, leading to diminution, untainted, not subject to fetters, not subject to ties, not subject to floods, not subject to yokes, not subject to hindrances, unclung-to, not subject to clinging, and non-defiled.
All phenomena are the recollection of the Buddha, the recollection of the Dhamma, and the recollection of the Saṅgha.

"Recollection of virtue, recollection of generosity, recollection of the deities, mindfulness of breathing, recollection of death, mindfulness occupied with the body, and recollection of peace—[are these all]?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
"Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness?"
“Yes.
“Then the eye-base is a foundation of mindfulness?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is the eye-base the foundation of mindfulness? Yes.
Is the eye-base mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, and the one-way path?
Is it leading to destruction, leading to enlightenment, leading to diminution, untainted, not conducive to fetters, ... [and so on] ... non-defiled;

and are the eye-base, the recollection of the Buddha, the recollection of the Dhamma, the recollection of the Saṅgha, the recollection of virtue, the recollection of generosity, the recollection of the deities, mindfulness of breathing, mindfulness of death, mindfulness directed to the body, and the recollection of peace [likewise]?
It should not be stated thus …pe… the ear-base … the nose-base …
The tongue base … the body base … the visible-form base …
the sense-sphere of sounds … the sense-sphere of odors … the sense-sphere of tastes …
The sphere of the tangible … lust … hatred …
delusion … conceit … views …
doubt … sloth … restlessness …
Is moral shame (*ahirika*) … and moral dread (*anottappa*) the establishment of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhāna*)?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
Is non-shame the establishment of mindfulness? Yes.
Is non-shame mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness …pe… bodily mindfulness, and the recollection of peace?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is mindfulness the foundations of mindfulness, and is that mindfulness itself? Yes.
Is the eye-base a foundation of mindfulness, and is that [foundation] mindfulness?
One should not say so... pe ...
Is mindfulness a foundation of mindfulness, and is that [foundation] mindfulness?
Yes. The ear-base … [and so on] … the body-base … [and so on] … the visible-form base … [and so on].
The sense-sphere of the tangible … lust … hatred … delusion … [and so on] … lack of moral dread is a foundation of mindfulness; and that mindfulness is [itself] mindfulness?
One should not say so … [and so on].
The eye-base is a foundation of mindfulness; and yet it is not mindfulness?
Yes. Mindfulness is a foundation of mindfulness; and yet it is not mindfulness? [Yes.]
It should not be stated thus … [and so on] … the ear-base … the body-base …
The sense-sphere of visible forms … [and so on] … the sense-sphere of tangible objects … lust …
Is hatred … delusion … [and so on] … lack of moral dread a foundation of mindfulness, yet it is not mindfulness?
“Yes,” you say.
“If there is mindfulness, is that mindfulness not itself an establishment of mindfulness?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it not to be said that "all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness"?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that mindfulness is established by taking all phenomena as its object?
Yes, it is.
If mindfulness is established by taking all phenomena as its object, then indeed, O friend, you must say this:
“All phenomena are foundations of mindfulness.
Is it because mindfulness is established by taking every phenomenon as its object that all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness? Yes.
If contact is established by taking all phenomena as its object, are all phenomena foundations of contact?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...If mindfulness is established by taking all phenomena as its object, are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness?
“Yes.
“Feeling is established with reference to all phenomena; perception is established with reference to all phenomena.”
If you say that volition stabilizes and consciousness stabilizes, and therefore all phenomena have consciousness as their foundation—
this should not be said... [and so on].
Are all phenomena the foundations of mindfulness? Yes.
All beings are possessed of established mindfulness, endowed with mindfulness, and grounded in mindfulness.
Is mindfulness established in all beings?
One should not say so … [as before] … Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness?
“Yes, [they do].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, those who do not enjoy mindfulness directed to the body do not enjoy the Deathless’?”
“Monks, those who enjoy mindfulness directed to the body enjoy the deathless.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Do all beings enjoy, acquire, practice, develop, and cultivate mindfulness directed to the body?
One should not say so… [as before] … Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness?
“Yes, [it is so].
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, this is the one-way path for the purification of beings, for the surmounting of sorrow and lamentation’?”
"For the cessation of suffering and grief, for the attainment of the true way, for the realization of Nibbāna— namely,
these four foundations of mindfulness.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are all phenomena the path with a single goal?
One should not speak thus… [and so on].
"All phenomena are foundations of mindfulness"? Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Monks, with the appearance of a wheel-turning monarch, there is the appearance of seven treasures. Which seven?
There is the appearance of the wheel-treasure; there is the appearance of the elephant-treasure; there is the appearance of the horse-treasure…”
of the jewel-treasure … of the woman-treasure … of the householder-treasure …
The appearance of the jewel of the counselor occurs.
Monks, with the appearance of a wheel-turning monarch, there is the appearance of these seven jewels.
Monks, with the appearance of a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, there is the appearance of the seven jewels of the factors of enlightenment.
Of which seven?
There is the manifestation of the jewel of the mindfulness factor of enlightenment; there is the manifestation of the jewel of the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment;
there is the manifestation of the jewel of the energy factor of enlightenment; there is the manifestation of the jewel of the rapture factor of enlightenment.
“There arises, bhikkhus, the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; there arises the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena;
there arises the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of energy; there arises the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of rapture;

there arises the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of tranquility; there arises the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of concentration; there arises the appearance of the jewel of the enlightenment factor of equanimity. With the appearance of the Tathāgata, bhikkhus, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, there is the appearance of these seven jewels of the factors of enlightenment.”
Is this indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Is it therefore the case that, with the appearance of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, all phenomena become the treasure of the mindfulness factor of enlightenment?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are all phenomena (dhammas) foundations of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhāna)? Yes.
All phenomena are right exertions … bases of psychic power … faculties …
"Is it the case that the *balas* are *bojjhaṅgas*?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
The Discourse on the Foundations of Mindfulness is finished.
